chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from al-Abbas, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Muhammad ibn 'Udhayfir, from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him):
Concerning a man — does his wudu become nullified if he sleeps while sitting? He said: 'If it is on Friday in the mosque, no wudu is required of him, for he is in a state of necessity.'

This report is to be understood as meaning that no wudu is required of him, but tayammum is required of him, as we will explain in the chapter on tayammum. He then mentioned — may Allah support him — after [the case of] sleep, the illness that prevents [the performance of] dhikr; and what I have been informed of is evidence for this.

key_terms.التَّيَمُّمُ: tayammum — dry ritual purification with earth, substituting for wudu when its normal performance is impossible
key_terms.النَّوْمِ: sleep — a recognised nullifier of wudu in Shia jurisprudence
key_terms.ضَرُورَةٍ: necessity (darura) — jurisprudential principle permitting relaxation of obligatory rulings
key_terms.وُضُوؤُهُ: his wudu — the ritual ablution potentially nullified by sleep

ai.seo_question: Does falling asleep while sitting on Friday in the mosque nullify one's wudu according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in Tahdhib al-Ahkam?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) through a chain of five narrators, addresses the jurisprudential question of whether sleeping while seated on Friday in the mosque nullifies a man's wudu. The Imam rules that no wudu is required in that circumstance due to a state of necessity (ḍarūra). Sheikh al-Tusi, the compiler, further interprets this as entailing the obligation of tayammum in place of wudu, to be elaborated in the dedicated chapter.
